java_findings: CommandLinkStateCommon.java:111 creates a Display with Display.getWithNewlines for state transition labels before LinkArg/SvekEdge consume it.
Display.getWithNewlines parses legacy \\n, \\l, \\r, \\t, and \\\\ outside raw <math>, <latex>, and [[link]] spans; \\l and \\r set Display.naturalHorizontalAlignment.
SvekEdge.java:286-293 resolves state link alignment through getMessageTextAlignment, then Display.create0 overrides that with Display.getNaturalHorizontalAlignment when present.

SheetBlock1 sizes and draws the Display-created stripes as one TextBlock. Empty Display rows are not equivalent to Rust's zero-width empty text: the generated Java SVGs for empty rows contain a nonbreaking-space text node with positive textLength.
rust_findings: TransitionLabel at 723af6 parses source into rows plus optional natural alignment and preserves raw spans for <math>, <latex>, and [[...]].

StateTransitionLabelBlock is shared by sizing, emission, SVEK label boxes, and painted bounds; the core scalar-line divergence found in state-transition-label-family-baseline/checker_courier_nested_multiline_tb is addressed for ordinary unequal rows.
No fresh checker fixture labels, fixture stems, include_str!/include_bytes! references, or mechanism-specific golden reads were found in the inspected parser/state renderer paths.

The empty-row path is not Java-equivalent. Rust passes an empty row to text_render::emit_text, whose empty-segment branch emits an empty <text> with textLength 0; Java's row is rendered as NBSP with measurable width and participates in alignment.

overfit_scan.mechanical_forbidden_patterns: No mechanism-specific fixture labels, stems, include_str!, include_bytes!, or coordinate keyed post-hoc SVG surgery found in the inspected TransitionLabel/state label block paths.
overfit_scan.constant_provenance: The reviewed mechanism uses existing SVEK margins/padding and text metrics helpers. I did not find a new unexplained fixture-shaped numeric constant in the inspected label-block code.

inputs.name: checker_default_center_unequal_tb
inputs.finding: Structurally equivalent. This confirms the core scalar-to-Display-row change for ordinary unequal rows in a flat top-to-bottom state diagram.

inputs.name: checker_left_empty_rows_nested_lr
inputs.finding: Rejecting counterexample. Java lays out the nested scope left-to-right and renders three label rows: 'head', an NBSP empty row with textLength 3.334, and 'very wide left aligned trailer'. Rust lays out a different vertical/autonomous shape and the corresponding label comparison shows the empty row as zero-width with shifted/missing row correspondence. This disproves the account's claim that every state rendering path sizes, routes, paints, and bounds the same parsed Display block for empty rows and nested/directional axes.

inputs.name: checker_right_empty_rows_selfloop_tb
inputs.finding: Rejecting counterexample with an isolated display-line failure. The only reported structural difference is the empty middle row: Java emits NBSP with textLength 4.9219 at x=275.5254, while Rust emits a zero-width empty text node at x=280.4473. This is squarely inside the Display-row model, not a broad layout failure.

inputs.name: checker_link_raw_escape_outside_newline_lr
inputs.finding: Rejecting counterexample. Java preserves the raw link href/title newline semantics inside [[...]] and splits the outside row; Rust emits comparable text rows but the no-oracle comparison fails with a vertical canvas and a literal-backslash title attribute where Java encodes a newline in the title. The raw-span axis is not accepted by exact shipping comparison.

inputs.name: checker_math_raw_escape_font_tb
inputs.finding: Rejecting counterexample. Java produces an embedded math image for the raw <math> span and a second text row. Rust emits only text for the second row in the compared position and the canvas/path/row geometry differs. The Java run printed a Batik ClassNotFoundException but still generated a well-formed SVG with an embedded math image; the pair remains preserved as a valid raw-span held-out failure.

inputs.name: checker_directional_up_down_default_alignment
inputs.finding: Structurally equivalent. This gives some confidence that ordinary directional arrows without left-to-right layout and without empty/raw rows consume the shared label block correctly.

inputs.name: checker_tab_backslash_unknown_escape_lr
inputs.finding: Rejecting counterexample. Java converts \\t into a tab advance, \\\\ into one backslash, preserves \\q, and splits the outside newline, but the exact no-oracle comparison fails with the same left-to-right vs vertical layout drift seen in other LR state fixtures. The escape-row content itself is largely consistent, but the mechanism's held-out LR axis is not green.

inputs.name: checker_alignment_order_last_marker_wins
inputs.finding: Structurally equivalent. This supports the source claim that later \\l/\\r markers overwrite the block-wide natural alignment.

summary.primary_reject_reason: The implementation does not yet model Java's empty Display row as a measurable NBSP atom; a self-loop fixture isolates this to one text element. Additional raw-span and left-to-right/nested held-out fixtures also fail exact no-oracle comparison.
recommended_next_account_focus: Trace Java's empty Display row through Sheet/Stripe/Atom creation to the emitted NBSP and apply the same model before measuring, aligning, emitting, and bounding transition label rows.

Separate the left-to-right state layout drift from Display-row correctness; either narrow the mechanism acceptance axes or fix the direction/autonomous path before claiming all listed perturbation axes.
Clarify raw link title escaping and raw math image support in the account's scope boundary so the held-out raw-span tests do not mask or excuse unrelated renderer gaps.
